questions.q: I ___ smoke, but I quit five years ago.
questions.why: 'Used to + infinitive' describes a past habit that is no longer true.

questions.q: She ___ living alone now; she enjoys the quiet.
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' means accustomed to or familiar with something.

questions.q: It took time, but I finally ___ driving on the left.
questions.why: 'Get used to + -ing' describes the process of becoming accustomed.

questions.q: When we were kids, we ___ play in the street for hours.
questions.why: 'Would' can describe repeated past actions, like 'used to' for habits.

questions.q: I ___ like vegetables when I was young, but I do now.
questions.why: In the negative, drop the '-d': 'didn't use to'.

questions.q: Are you ___ the cold weather here yet?
questions.why: 'Be used to + noun/-ing' means accustomed to; here it's followed by a noun.

questions.q: There ___ be a cinema here, but they knocked it down.
questions.why: 'Used to' describes a past state that no longer exists.

questions.q: He's a nurse, so he ___ working nights.
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' shows he is accustomed to night shifts.

questions.q: Did you ___ have long hair?
questions.why: In questions with 'did', use the base form 'use to'.

questions.q: After a month, she ___ to the spicy food.
questions.why: 'Got used to' shows the gradual process of becoming accustomed.

questions.q: My grandfather ___ tell us stories every evening.
questions.why: 'Would' expresses a repeated past action or habit.

questions.q: I'm not ___ getting up so early.
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' for familiarity; the negative is 'not used to'.

questions.q: We ___ have a dog when I was a child.
questions.why: 'Used to' describes a past situation that is no longer true.

questions.q: It was hard at first, but he's ___ the noise now.
questions.why: 'Be used to + noun' means accustomed to: used to the noise.

questions.q: How do you ___ working from home?
questions.why: 'Get used to' refers to the process of becoming accustomed.

questions.q: She ___ be very shy, but now she's confident.
questions.why: Use 'used to' for a past state; 'would' is avoided with state verbs like 'be'.

questions.q: They aren't ___ such cold winters.
questions.why: 'Be used to + noun' for familiarity; negative form keeps 'used to'.

questions.q: I ___ to the long commute after a few weeks.
questions.why: 'Got used to' shows becoming accustomed over time.

questions.q: ___ you use to live in London?
questions.why: Questions about past habits use 'did' + 'use to'.

questions.q: As a boy, he ___ spend summers at the lake.
questions.why: 'Would' describes a repeated action in the past, like a habit.

questions.q: Now that she's a teacher, she ___ speaking in public.
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' means she is comfortable with it now.

questions.q: I can't ___ this hot climate.
questions.why: 'Get used to' refers to the (here, difficult) process of adjusting.

questions.q: We ___ have much money, so we never travelled.
questions.why: The negative past habit form is 'didn't use to' (no '-d').

questions.q: He ___ wearing glasses now; they don't bother him.
questions.why: 'Be used to + -ing' shows present familiarity.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I ___ to play tennis every Sunday, but I stopped.' (past habit)
questions.why: 'Used to + infinitive' expresses a discontinued past habit.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She is used to ___ (work) long hours.'
questions.why: After 'be used to' we use the -ing form.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'It took a while, but I got used to ___ (drive) on the right.'
questions.why: 'Get used to' is followed by the -ing form.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'They didn't ___ to have a car.' (negative past habit)
questions.why: In the negative, the form is 'didn't use to' without the '-d'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'When I was young, I ___ (would, habit) walk to school every day.' Give the modal.
questions.why: 'Would' describes repeated past actions or habits.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Are you used ___ the weather here?' (preposition)
questions.why: 'Be used to' always takes the preposition 'to' before a noun or -ing.

questions.q: I ___ coffee, but now I love it.
questions.why: After 'didn't', use the base form 'use to' (no d).

questions.q: She's not ___ up early.
questions.why: 'Be used to' + -ing means 'be accustomed to'.

questions.q: There ___ be a cinema here.
questions.why: 'Used to' + base verb for past states that are no longer true.

questions.q: He'll soon get ___ in the city.
questions.why: 'Get used to' + -ing describes becoming accustomed.

questions.q: ___ you use to play chess?
questions.why: Questions about past habits: 'Did you use to…?'
